The reversible logic gate is utilized to optimize power consumption by a feature of retrieving input logic from an output logic because of bijective mapping between input and output.
The proposed inventive0 gate has a hardware complexity of 7α+4β+3δ and a quantum cost of 10.
The proposed 4:2 reversible compressor circuit contains 2 inventive0 gates and has a quantum cost of 20.
The proposed 5:2 reversible compressor circuit contains 3 inventive0 gates and has a quantum cost of 30.
The total logical calculation (T) for the 4:2 compressor circuit is 6, and for the 5:2 compressor circuit is 21α+12β+9δ.
The 4:2 compressor circuit generates at least 4 garbage outputs, and the n:2 compressor circuit generates at least (2n-4) garbage outputs.
The 4:2 compressor circuit requires 2 ancilla inputs, and the n:2 compressor circuit requires at least (n-2) ancilla inputs.
The proposed compressor circuits outperform existing designs in terms of garbage outputs, number of gates, and quantum cost.
The compressor can reduce the effect of carry (produced from full adder) in arithmetic frame design.
The authors implemented basic reversible gates like CNOT, TG, F2G, PG, FRG, BJN, and URG in MOS transistors using the Gate Diffusion Input (GDI) technique.
The MOS transistor count for the basic reversible gates is provided, showing the efficiency of the GDI-based implementation.
The compressor structure can be used in low-power circuits, ALUs, and quantum computers.

The authors propose an algorithm for designing a compressor structure and provide lemmas related to the number of gates, quantum cost, garbage outputs, and ancilla inputs for an n:2 reversible compressor.
The comparative analysis table shows that the proposed 4:2 compressor circuit outperforms existing designs.
The authors conclude that the proposed compressor circuits will be useful in low-power VLSI circuit design, arithmetic logic units, and quantum computers.
